Hypovolaemic shock is where blood flow to tissues is insufficient to meet metabolic requirements.

Metabolic acidosis occurs when the bodies pH drops below 7.35 due to depletion of HCO3 or accumulation of H+/acids.

Hypovolaemia → ↓O2 Delivery due to Oxygen flux equation = SpO2xHbx1.34 + (0.003xPaO2)

Relative tissue hypoxia caused by shock results in aerobic respiration being unable to take place and subsequently lactate is produced from pyruvate to recycle NAH+ to produce ATP. 

In type 1 lactic acidosis lactate accumulates due to hepatic hypoperfusion Where lactate is unable to be metabolised in the cori cycle. 

Consequences of Metabolic acidosis:

- Respiratory 

  > ↓pH → Stimulation of peripheral chemoreceptors →  ↑MV (3L for each 1mmHg EtCO2)    
  >
  > → ↑MV → ↑respiratory metabolic requirements 

- Cardiovascular 

  ↓pH → (↓ inotropy, ↓ SVR, ↑PVR) → ↓mAP and CO

- Right Shift of oxyhaemoglobin curve 

- Enzymatic dysfunction 

  > Many physiological enzymes required for Normal body function require tight balance of pH to maintain function. In deranged pH enzymatic function may be reduced or non-functional.

- Metabolic

  ↑H+
